# Education

Each row is one entry, each column a field. `fields` renames a column the
style does not expect, like `dplyr::rename()`.

::: {.entries style="detailed" fields="{what: Degree, with: Institution, when: Years, where: Location}"}
| Degree             | Institution         | Years     | Location      |
|--------------------|---------------------|-----------|---------------|
| Ph.D. in Physics   | University of Paris | 1891-1895 | Paris, France |
| M.Sc. in Chemistry | University of Paris | 1889-1891 | Paris, France |
:::

# Employment

A grid table can hold a bullet list in a cell, so `why` carries several points
per entry. Here the headings already match, and no `fields` is needed.

::: {.entries style="detailed"}
+------------+---------------------+-----------+------------------------------+
| what       | with                | when      | why                          |
+============+=====================+===========+==============================+
| Professor  | University of Paris | 1906-1934 | - First woman to hold the    |
|            |                     |           |   chair of General Physics   |
|            |                     |           | - Directed the Curie         |
|            |                     |           |   Laboratory                 |
+------------+---------------------+-----------+------------------------------+
| Researcher | EPCI                | 1897-1906 | - Isolated polonium and      |
|            |                     |           |   radium                     |
+------------+---------------------+-----------+------------------------------+
:::

# Awards

The `brief` style is a single line per entry, for lists needing no
elaboration.

::: {.entries style="brief"}
| what                     | where           | when |
|--------------------------|-----------------|------|
| Nobel Prize in Chemistry | Swedish Academy | 1911 |
| Davy Medal               | Royal Society   | 1903 |
| Nobel Prize in Physics   | Swedish Academy | 1903 |
:::

# Service

Markdown inside cells is preserved and LaTeX special characters are escaped,
so *emphasis* and a literal 100% both come out right.

::: {.entries style="brief"}
| what                                 | where    | when |
|--------------------------------------|----------|------|
| Member, *Solvay Council*             | Brussels | 1911 |
| Director, Red Cross Radiology (100%) | Paris    | 1914 |
:::

# Fields of Research

The `skills` style pairs a category with its members, rendered here as a
labelled group of tags. Each member is its own tag when `why` is a bulleted
list, or one tag holding the whole line when `with` is a single string.

::: {.entries style="skills"}
+----------------+-----------------------------+
| what           | why                         |
+================+=============================+
| Radiochemistry | - Fractional crystallisation|
|                | - Isolation of radium       |
+----------------+-----------------------------+
| Electrometry   | - Piezoelectric quartz      |
+----------------+-----------------------------+
:::

# Strengths

The `badges` style prints one pill per entry from `what`, with no grouping
heading above them -- unlike `skills`, which labels a run of tags with a
category.

::: {.entries style="badges"}
| what                        |
|------------------------------|
| Meticulous experimentalist  |
| Methodical                  |
| Tenacious                   |
:::

# Referees

The `cards` style draws a reference card per entry: `what` as a bold name,
`with` on a line marked by an "@" icon, and `why` on a line marked by an
envelope icon.

::: {.entries style="cards"}
| what                  | with                        | why                                          |
|-----------------------|------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------|
| Prof. Henri Becquerel | h.becquerel@sorbonne.fr     | Muséum national d'Histoire naturelle, Paris  |
| Prof. André Debierne  | a.debierne@sorbonne.fr      | Institut du Radium, Paris                    |
:::
